newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU aids Dutch piglet slaughter to combat swine fever.
newsitem.headline: EU aids Dutch piglet slaughter to combat swine fever.

text.p: The European Union on Monday approved aid to slaughter 500,000 piglets under three weeks old in the Netherlands because of continuing outbreaks of swine fever, a Commission spokesman said.
The EU's pig management committee agreed to buy-in the animals at a price of 38 ecus per animal.
Around one million pigs have so far been slaughtered in the Netherlands in a bid to control the highly contagious disease which is not harmful to humans.
Last week the number of outbreaks of the disease in the Netherlands rose to 133 and the Dutch government asked for EU support for the slaughter of five million animals, the spokesman added.

"The Dutch asked for our support for the purchase of five million very young pigs but the management committee accepted only 500,000, for the moment. The Commission will pay 70 per cent of the cost," the spokesman said.
The committee also approved a programme to buy-in 132,000 fattening pigs and 60,000 piglets from the Catalonia region of Spain where swine fever restrictions were imposed last month.
The Commission will pay 70 percent of the estimated 50 to 69 ecus cost per animal slaughtered in the region which has suffered 17 cases of swine fever, the spokesman added.
Aid for buying in piglets in Germany is to be increased from 62 ecus to 74 ecus per animal as a market support measure following earlier outbreaks of swine fever.
"There have been no new outbreaks in Germany. All these measures are market support measures," the spokesman added.
